_comment: Everything about the assistant EXCEPT provider choices (stack.json) and tools (tools.json). deploy.mjs merges all three, injects prompt.md as the system message, and substitutes {{ENV_VARS}}.
name: BrightConnect — Ava
firstMessage: Hi, thanks for calling BrightConnect. I'm Ava. What can I help you with today?

startSpeakingPlan._comment: Deliberately NO smartEndpointingPlan. Flux does end-of-turn detection natively inside the ASR; stacking Vapi's endpointing on top would mean two systems deciding the same thing and adds latency for nothing. waitSeconds is a small floor so a caller drawing breath mid-sentence is not cut off.

stopSpeakingPlan._comment: Barge-in. numWords 0 means interrupt on any speech rather than waiting for the caller to produce N words. An agent that talks over an interruption is the fastest way to make someone ask for a human.

idleMessages: I can't hear anything — are you still with me?

_maxDurationComment: Cost guardrail. The demo page is public, so an unbounded call length is an unbounded bill.
_noEndCallPhrases: endCallPhrases is deliberately absent. It is a substring matcher that hangs up whenever the ASSISTANT utters a listed phrase — and an earlier version listed 'thanks for calling BrightConnect', which appears verbatim in firstMessage, so Ava hung up on her own greeting. Termination is the endCall tool's job: the model decides explicitly, and silenceTimeoutSeconds and maxDurationSeconds are the backstops. Do not re-add this field. deploy.mjs will refuse to deploy if a phrase here collides with firstMessage.

analysisPlan._comment: Post-call QA loop. Without structured output you cannot answer 'what fraction of calls did the bot actually resolve' — which is the only number that tells you whether the design works.

resolved.description: True if the bot resolved the request without a human.

escalated.description: True if the call was handed to a human.

escalationReason.description: The reason passed to escalateToHuman, or empty if not escalated.

toolsUsed.description: Names of the tools called during this conversation.

customerSentiment.description: The customer's tone by the end of the call.

noMatchCount.description: How many times the bot failed to understand the customer.
